## Why
Epic polite-antivirus-bedbug (`536b-8930-b922-4063`) has an acceptance box that reads: "docs/concurrency.md §I1 moved 'implemented'; residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed". On origin/main 9d10232dd89, two places are out of date:
- The `.retired` lifecycle paragraph in docs/concurrency.md §I1 (lines 61-75) still says the history reclamation "is specified by **ADR 0106**".
- ADR 0106's Follow-up section (docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md:222-225) still calls that note "*specified, in-progress*".

The reclamation is built, and it was run against production `tickets` on 2026-11-20 18:14 PST.

## What changes
No code, config key, env var, flag or test changes.

1. **docs/concurrency.md §I1.** Replace the "**`.retired` lifecycle.**" paragraph text, from line 61 up to (not including) the sentence "`.retired` files are **benign under a code rollback**", with the block below, committed exactly as written here (same line breaks). The "benign under a code rollback" sentence and everything after it stay unchanged, starting a new paragraph after the block. The old paragraph's sentence "`.retired` files are blobs and the pack the CI budget guards is blobless, so reclaiming them removes ~0 from that pack" goes away. It is wrong today because the `verify-identity.yml` budget measures only the code checkout, not `tickets` (cc4a23a2405, ticket bc25-1351).

```markdown
**`.retired` lifecycle.** Retired files stay in the working tree permanently. That
storage tradeoff guarantees a folded source is never lost and can never be resurrected
into a `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`. No branch-wide `.retired` sweep exists. Story
`mystical-capsizable-ibis` was closed wontfix by operator decision on 2026-11-18,
because the real-data dry run reached its pack reduction without one and the
sweep's plan review blocked on fsck `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES`, snapshot-rebuild
refusal and retired-event readers. The pack lever is
**remote-anchored below-horizon commit/tree history reclamation** (ADR 0106,
`docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md`), and it is implemented.
It is safe only past causal stability, meaning once no clone can still be
mid-reconvergence against the pre-compaction events. ADR 0106 makes that condition
precise as the C1–C5 boundary at the commit/tree level. The implementation is split
across 7 modules:
- `rebar._store.reclaim_eligibility`: the `[reclaim].horizon_days` remote-reachability check.
- `rebar._commands.reclaim_collapse`: the core-git collapse, with authorship-ledger
  `position→commit_sha` re-resolution and the `enforce_since` re-anchor.
- `rebar._commands.reclaim_collapse_stream`: the long-lived `fast-import` and
  `cat-file` sessions the collapse runs on.
- `rebar._commands.reclaim_resign`: re-signs failing events during the collapse.
- `rebar._commands.reclaim_publish`: the lease-guarded publish-swap, the S3 bundle-set
  replacement, and rollback.
- `rebar._commands.reclaim_dry_run`: the shadow-clone dry-run harness.
- `rebar._store.stale_override`: the reconnect override.

The reconnect and publish protocols are the paragraphs "Reconnect after a history
reclaim" and "Publishing a reclaimed baseline" under Inbound — background sync.
The reclamation was run on 2026-11-20 at 18:14 PST, under epic `polite-antivirus-bedbug`
(`536b-8930-b922-4063`). It was one lease-guarded atomic push that moved `tickets` from
`efcf5ae2b97` to `6a6dda16fc7`, and it left the backup ref
`refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-20261121T021044Z` at the old tip. Commits went from
312,156 to 14,235. On the proof's fake remote, the blobless pack went from
625 MiB to 108 MiB. **Measured residual:** a fresh blobless bare clone of origin
`tickets` at `4fd8b099490` (14,375 commits), taken 2026-11-20 at 21:13 PST, has
`size-pack` 122,794 KiB (about 120 MiB). The residual grows with write volume until
the next reclaim. No CI budget applies to it: the `verify-identity.yml` pack budget
(102,400 KiB) measures only the code checkout, which excludes `tickets` (`cc4a23a2405`).
```

2. **docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md, `## Follow-up`.** Replace its single paragraph (lines 222-225) with:

```markdown
`docs/concurrency.md` §I1's `.retired` lifecycle note is promoted from a *follow-up* to an
*implemented* model. It cross-references this ADR as the reclamation contract and records
the 2026-11-20 production run and its measured residual pack. Implementation was delivered
by stories **S1** (collapse engine + ledger reconciliation), **S2** (publish-swap + rollback)
and **S3** (dry-run harness) under epic `536b`.
```

Where each fact comes from:
- Run, tips, backup ref, commit counts and the 625 -> 108 MiB fake-remote pack: comments "Published re-signed, collapsed tickets history" and "Real-data re-sign proof" on polite-antivirus-bedbug.
- Residual: `git clone --bare --filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch tickets https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` then `git count-objects -v` (size-pack 122794), 2026-11-20 21:13 PST, tip 4fd8b099490, `rev-list --count` 14375.
- Wontfix reason: mystical-capsizable-ibis close_reason.
- Module list: `ls src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_*.py src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py src/rebar/_store/stale_override.py`, 7 files.
- Budget scope: commit cc4a23a2405.
- The 2 cross-referenced paragraphs exist under `### Inbound — background sync` (docs/concurrency.md:797 and :822).

## Acceptance Criteria
All proofs run from the worktree root after the edit. `I1` below means the output of `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md`.
- [ ] I1 says the reclamation is implemented: `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | grep -c 'and it is implemented'` prints 1.
- [ ] I1 names all 7 modules: each of `reclaim_eligibility`, `reclaim_collapse\``, `reclaim_collapse_stream`, `reclaim_resign`, `reclaim_publish`, `reclaim_dry_run` and `stale_override` greps at least once in I1.
- [ ] I1 points to the 2 existing paragraphs: I1 contains `under Inbound — background sync`, and `grep -c 'Reconnect after a history reclaim (ADR 0106\|Publishing a reclaimed baseline, and rolling it back' docs/concurrency.md` prints 2.
- [ ] I1 records the run: I1 contains each of `2026-11-20 at 18:14 PST`, `efcf5ae2b97`, `6a6dda16fc7`, `refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-20261121T021044Z`, `312,156` and `14,235`.
- [ ] I1 records the fake-remote pack: I1 contains `625 MiB to 108 MiB`.
- [ ] I1 records the measured residual: I1 contains `122,794 KiB`, `4fd8b099490` and `14,375 commits`.
- [ ] I1 says the residual grows: I1 contains `grows with write volume`.
- [ ] I1 says the budget excludes `tickets`: I1 contains `cc4a23a2405`.
- [ ] I1 gives the recorded wontfix reason: I1 contains `mystical-capsizable-ibis` and `operator decision on 2026-11-18`.
- [ ] The old wording is gone: `grep -cF 'is specified by **ADR 0106**' docs/concurrency.md` prints 0.
- [ ] The old budget sentence is gone: `grep -cF 'the pack the CI budget guards is blobless' docs/concurrency.md` prints 0.
- [ ] The rollback sentence survives: I1 contains `benign under a code rollback`.
- [ ] Only the planned regions change: `git diff -U0 origin/main --stat` lists exactly docs/concurrency.md and docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md. Every `@@` hunk header in `git diff -U0 origin/main -- docs/concurrency.md` starts at a line between 61 and 80. Every hunk in the ADR diff starts at line 222 or later.
- [ ] The ADR Follow-up is updated: `grep -c 'specified, in-progress' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` prints 0, and `grep -c '\*implemented\* model' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` prints 1.
- [ ] `make verify` passes, or each failure is shown to be environmental.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The Gerrit change gets `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on its current patch set with 0 unresolved comments, and it merges to main. Evidence recorded on this ticket: change number, patch-set SHA, vote outcome and merged SHA on origin/main.
  provenance: environment=developer-workstation-worktree; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — votes are read from the Gerrit REST API, and the merge is confirmed with `git branch -r --contains` on origin/main.

## File impact
- `docs/concurrency.md`: the §I1 `.retired` lifecycle paragraph only.
- `docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md`: the `## Follow-up` paragraph only.

## Portability
Documentation only. Nothing depends on a CI provider.

## Testing
Documentation-only change, so no new test is needed. The AC commands above are the proof, run before commit. `make verify` covers the docs-drift, ADR-index and doc-policy tests.
